author: Luke the Evangelist
original: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν Ἰησοῦς ἀρχόμενος ὡσεὶ ἐτῶν τριάκοντα, ὢν υἱός, ὡς ἐνομίζετο, Ἰωσήφ τοῦ Ἡλεί
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli,
translator: King James Version (1611), as shown on Biblehub
edition: Biblehub: https://biblehub.com/text/luke/3-23.htm (Greek box and KJV line)
what_it_says: Jesus, being (as was supposed) son of Joseph, is called son of Heli; the Westcott-Hort Greek has no article before Ἰωσήφ.
limits: The brief's string (Ἠλὶ, Ἰωσὴφ τοῦ Ἠλὶ) matches the Textus Receptus line on Biblehub, not W-H; Nestle 1904 and Tischendorf 8th print Ἰωσὴφ τοῦ Ἡλεὶ with no article before Ἰωσὴφ; the W-H line is from Biblehub, not an open scan of W-H.

work: A Commentary on the Gospel of St. Luke, vol. 1
author: Frédéric Louis Godet
ref: Luke 3:23 (comment on the article and on tou Heli)
original: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν Ἰησοῦς ἀρχόμενος ὡσεὶ ἐτῶν τριάκοντα, ὢν υἱός, ὡς ἐνομίζετο, Ἰωσήφ τοῦ Ἡλεί
original_edition: Greek of the commented verse, see G6-01 (WH via Biblehub)
english: This want of the article puts the name Joseph outside the genealogical series properly so called, and assigns to it a peculiar position. We must conclude from it — 1st. That this name belongs rather to the sentence introduced by Luke; 2d. That the genealogical document which he consulted began with the name of Heli; 3d. And consequently, that this piece was not originally the genealogy of Jesus or of Joseph, but of Heli. [...] The genitive [Greek omitted], of Heli, depends therefore not on Joseph, but on the word son.
translator: E. W. Shalders (from the 2nd French ed.)
edition: T. & T. Clark, Edinburgh, 1875; archive.org identifier commentaryongo01gode (text layer read)
what_it_says: Godet argues from the missing article before Joseph that the list began with Heli and that tou Heli depends on 'son', not on Joseph.
limits: A grammatical argument only; it does not by itself say Heli was Mary's father. The phrase '3d.' is inferred from the OCR ('od.'); check the image. Godet's own reading is that the list is Heli's.

work: A Commentary on the Gospel of St. Luke, vol. 1
author: Frédéric Louis Godet
ref: Luke 3:23 (comment, Heli as Mary's line; Talmud claim)
original: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν Ἰησοῦς ἀρχόμενος ὡσεὶ ἐτῶν τριάκοντα, ὢν υἱός, ὡς ἐνομίζετο, Ἰωσήφ τοῦ Ἡλεί
original_edition: Greek of the commented verse, see G6-01 (WH via Biblehub)
english: This study of the text in detail leads us in this way to admit — 1. That the genealogical register of Luke is that of Heli, the grandfather of Jesus; 2. That, this affiliation of Jesus by Heli being expressly opposed to His affiliation by Joseph, the document which he has preserved for us can be nothing else in his view than the genealogy of Jesus through Mary. [...] It is remarkable that, in the Talmud, Mary the mother of Jesus is called the daughter of Heli (Chagiga 77. 4).
what_it_says: Godet holds that Luke gives Heli's line, and so Mary's genealogy, and cites a Talmud passage calling Mary daughter of Heli.
limits: The Talmud citation could not be confirmed: Sefaria texts searched (Jerusalem Talmud Hagigah 2:2 and 2:1, Babylonian Talmud Hagigah 4b, Sanhedrin 106a, Ketubot 66a) have no 'Miriam daughter of Eli/Heli'. Godet's 'Chagiga 77.4' location was not identified. Godet also treats 'son' as 'grandson' here.

work: Word Pictures in the New Testament, vol. 2 (Luke)
author: Archibald Thomas Robertson
original: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν Ἰησοῦς ἀρχόμενος ὡσεὶ ἐτῶν τριάκοντα, ὢν υἱός, ὡς ἐνομίζετο, Ἰωσήφ τοῦ Ἡλεί
original_edition: Greek of the commented verse, see G6-01 (WH via Biblehub)
english: Joseph, of course, did not have two fathers. If we understand Luke to be giving the real genealogy of Jesus through Mary, the matter is simple enough. [...] It was equally natural for Luke, a Greek himself and writing for the whole world, to give the actual genealogy of Jesus through Mary.
edition: Scan 'wordpicturesinne0002arch_l4x8' (The Gospel According to Luke), 1930; text layer read
what_it_says: Robertson takes the Luke-through-Mary reading as the simple solution and calls it natural for Luke.
limits: Robertson gives no evidence for the claim; he says Plummer objects to the sense 'son' used twice. He treats it as a preference, not a proof.

work: A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Gospel according to St. Luke (ICC)
author: Alfred Plummer
original: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν Ἰησοῦς ἀρχόμενος ὡσεὶ ἐτῶν τριάκοντα, ὢν υἱός, ὡς ἐνομίζετο, Ἰωσήφ τοῦ Ἡλεί
original_edition: Greek of the commented verse, see G6-01 (WH via Biblehub)
english: But this solution is not suggested by anyone until Annius of Viterbo propounded it, c. A.D. 1490.
edition: T. & T. Clark, ICC (scan 'internationalcri0000stlu', edition line not read)
what_it_says: Plummer says the Luke-is-Mary solution was first proposed by Annius of Viterbo, which he dates c. 1490.
limits: Plummer dates Annius to c. 1490, not 1498 as the brief states; this is his judgment about the solutions he surveyed, not a full survey of medieval writers. Plummer names Julius Africanus's levirate explanation as the earliest; he does not say Africanus gave a Mary reading.
memory_only: The 1498 date in the brief is not confirmed by this source.

work: A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Gospel according to St. Luke (ICC)
author: Alfred Plummer
original: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν Ἰησοῦς ἀρχόμενος ὡσεὶ ἐτῶν τριάκοντα, ὢν υἱός, ὡς ἐνομίζετο, Ἰωσήφ τοῦ Ἡλεί
original_edition: Greek of the commented verse, see G6-01 (WH via Biblehub)
english: It is evident from the wording that Lk. is here giving the genealogy of Joseph and [text layer garbled] of Mary. In the eye of the law Jesus was the heir of Joseph; and therefore it is Joseph's descent which is of importance. Mary may have been the daughter of Heli; but, if she was, Lk. ignores the fact.
edition: T. & T. Clark, ICC; archive.org internationalcri0000stlu
what_it_says: Plummer reads Luke as Joseph's genealogy, and treats Mary as Heli's daughter as possible but not stated.
limits: The words after 'Joseph and' are garbled in the text layer; the OCR reads 'пої'. The sense is probably 'not'. Check the image before quoting. He leaves the question open.

work: A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Gospel according to St. Luke (ICC)
author: Alfred Plummer
original: τοῦ Μαάθ τοῦ Ματταθίου τοῦ Σεμεείν τοῦ Ἰωσήχ τοῦ Ἰωδά τοῦ Ἰωανάν τοῦ Ῥησά τοῦ Ζοροβάβελ τοῦ Σαλαθιήλ τοῦ Νηρεί
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: Which was the son of Maath, which was the son of Mattathias, which was the son of Semei, which was the son of Joseph, which was the son of Juda, Which was the son of Joanna, which was the son of Rhesa, which was the son of Zorobabel, which was the son of Salathiel, which was the son of Neri, | Plummer: It is highly improbable that these are different persons from the Zerubbabel and the Shealtiel of Mt. i. 12.
what_it_says: Plummer holds that the Zerubbabel and Shealtiel of Luke 3:27 are the same as in Matthew 1:12, against a second pair of persons.
limits: Plummer himself says the two-Shealtiel hypothesis was adopted by Hottinger and Voss; he also gives the 1 Chr 3:19 (Pedaiah) explanation for Zerubbabel. Not a complete answer to the Shealtiel problem.

author: Luke the Evangelist
original: τοῦ Συμεών τοῦ Ἰούδα τοῦ Ἰωσήφ τοῦ Ἰωνάμ τοῦ Ἐλιακείμ τοῦ Μελεά τοῦ Μεννά τοῦ Ματταθά τοῦ Ναθάμ τοῦ Δαυείδ
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: Which was the son of Simeon, which was the son of Juda, which was the son of Joseph, which was the son of Jonan, which was the son of Eliakim, Which was the son of Melea, which was the son of Menan, which was the son of Mattatha, which was the son of Nathan, which was the son of David,
what_it_says: Luke's list runs through Nathan son of David rather than Solomon.
limits: Text only. The Nathan-line argument is in Eusebius HE 1.7 (see G6-27).

author: Luke the Evangelist
original: τοῦ Σερούχ τοῦ Ῥαγαύ τοῦ Φάλεκ τοῦ Ἔβερ τοῦ Σαλά τοῦ Καινάμ τοῦ Ἀρφαξάδ τοῦ Σήμ τοῦ Νῶε τοῦ Λάμεχ
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: Which was the son of Saruch, which was the son of Ragau, which was the son of Phalec, which was the son of Heber, which was the son of Sala, Which was the son of Cainan, which was the son of Arphaxad, which was the son of Sem, which was the son of Noe, which was the son of Lamech,
what_it_says: Luke 3:36 names Cainan between Arphaxad and Sala's line, i.e. Luke's text has a Cainan the Hebrew Genesis lacks.
limits: Biblehub line shows no brackets for Cainan; NA28 bracket status was not checked. The Cainan of Luke 3:37 is a separate name. See G6-11 to G6-13 for LXX and MT.

author: Luke the Evangelist
original: τοῦ Μαθουσαλά τοῦ Ἑνώχ τοῦ Ἰάρετ τοῦ Μαλελεήλ τοῦ Καινάμ τοῦ Ἐνώς τοῦ Σήθ τοῦ Ἀδάμ τοῦ θεοῦ.
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: Which was the son of Mathusala, which was the son of Enoch, which was the son of Jared, which was the son of Maleleel, which was the son of Cainan, Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.
what_it_says: The list ends at Adam, son of God (τοῦ θεοῦ), with no 'begat' before Adam.
limits: Eusebius HE 1.7.10 reads the same ending as a sign that the list is by law (see G6-27 and G6-28 references).

author: Septuagint translators
original: Καὶ ἔζησεν Ἀρφαξὰδ ἑκατὸν τριάκοντα πέντε ἔτη, καὶ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Καινάν. Καὶ ἔζησεν Ἀρφαξὰδ μετὰ τὸ γεννῆσαι αὐτὸν τὸν Καινὰν ἔτη τετρακόσια τριάκοντα, καὶ ἐγέννησεν υἱοὺς καὶ θυγατέρας, καὶ ἀπέθανεν.
original_edition: H. B. Swete, The Old Testament in Greek, vol. 1 (Cambridge 1887), PDF p. 49, text layer read as OCR (djvu). OCR puts a colon in 'τὸν: Καινάν' (removed here). Rahlfs 1935 vol. I (archive.org djvu OCR) agrees on 'Καιναν'.
english: And Arphaxad lived a hundred and thirty-five years, and begot Cainan. 13 And Arphaxad lived after he had begotten Cainan, four hundred years, and begot sons and daughters, and died.
page: PDF p. 15 of the Brenton scan; printed page not read
edition: Brenton, The Septuagint Version (London: Bagster 1851), archive.org 'OC LXX ... Brenton (1851) [ebible.org]'
what_it_says: The LXX has Arphaxad begetting Cainan (Kainan) at Gen 11:12, so it matches Luke 3:36 where the MT does not.
limits: Brenton's text prints 'Canaan lived after he had begotten Sala' at 11:13 (a misprint, not a different name). The Swete Greek is read from OCR, and the final letter of Καινάν is not confirmed at image resolution; I saw PDF p. 49 only at low zoom.

author: Septuagint translators
ref: LXX Genesis 10:24 (Cainan in the LXX, not in the MT)
original: καὶ Αρφαξαδ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Καιναν, καὶ Καιναν ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαλα, Σαλα δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Εβερ.
original_edition: Rahlfs, Septuaginta vol. I (1935), archive.org djvu OCR (no accents recovered); cross-check Swete vol. 1 OCR shows 'ἐγέννησεν τὸν Καινάμ, καὶ Καινὰμ ἐγέννησεν' (OCR)
english: And Arphaxad begot Cainan, and Cainan begot Sala. And Sala begot Heber.
page: PDF p. 15 of the Brenton scan; printed page not read
what_it_says: The LXX inserts Cainan in Gen 10:24 as well as Gen 11:12-13.
limits: Greek from OCR (no accents); the Swete PDF page for 10:24 was not located, so no PDF page is given.

author: Moses (traditional); Masoretic text
original: וְאַרְפַּכְשַׁ֖ד יָלַ֣ד אֶת־שָׁ֑לַח וְשֶׁ֖לַח יָלַ֥ד אֶת־עֵֽבֶר׃ וְאַרְפַּכְשַׁ֣ד חַ֔י חָמֵ֥שׁ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֖וֹלֶד אֶת־שָֽׁלַח׃ וַיְחִ֣י אַרְפַּכְשַׁ֗ד אַֽחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־שֶׁ֔לַח שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים וְאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד בָּנִ֖ים וּבָנֽוֹת׃ {ס}
original_edition: Sefaria, 'Miqra according to the Masorah' (Hebrew text as served by sefaria.org/api/texts/Genesis.10.24 and Genesis.11.12-13)
english: Arpachshad begot Shelah, and Shelah begot Eber. | When Arpachshad had lived 35 years, he begot Shelah. | After the birth of Shelah, Arpachshad lived 403 years and begot sons and daughters.
translator: JPS Tanakh, Gender-Sensitive Edition (as on Sefaria)
edition: Sefaria API; Biblehub Hebrew (same consonants) for 11:12
what_it_says: The Hebrew text has no Cainan in Gen 10:24 or 11:12-13; it goes Arpachshad, Shelah, Eber.
limits: Sefaria's Hebrew edition is labelled only as 'Miqra according to the Masorah'; I did not identify the manuscript. The Hebrew lacks Cainan, which is why Luke 3:36 is an objection point.

author: Luke the Evangelist
original: Ἐν δὲ τῷ μηνὶ τῷ ἕκτῳ ἀπεστάλη ὁ ἄγγελος Γαβριὴλ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς πόλιν τῆς Γαλιλαίας ᾗ ὄνομα Ναζαρὲτ πρὸς παρθένον ἐμνηστευμένην ἀνδρὶ ᾧ ὄνομα Ἰωσὴφ ἐξ οἴκου Δαυείδ, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τῆς παρθένου Μαριάμ.
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: And in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth, To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary.
what_it_says: The phrase 'of the house of David' follows Joseph's name; grammar does not decide whether it modifies Joseph or the virgin.
limits: Commentators disagree (see G6-14 and G6-15).

work: A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Gospel according to St. Luke (ICC)
author: Alfred Plummer
ref: Luke 1:27 (Plummer on the grammar and Mary's descent)
original: Ἐν δὲ τῷ μηνὶ τῷ ἕκτῳ ἀπεστάλη ὁ ἄγγελος Γαβριὴλ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς πόλιν τῆς Γαλιλαίας ᾗ ὄνομα Ναζαρὲτ πρὸς παρθένον ἐμνηστευμένην ἀνδρὶ ᾧ ὄνομα Ἰωσὴφ ἐξ οἴκου Δαυείδ, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τῆς παρθένου Μαριάμ.
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: It is unnecessary, and indeed impossible, to decide whether these words go with [Greek omitted], or with [Greek omitted], or with both. The last is the least probable, but Chrysostom and Wieseler support it. From 27. 32 and 69 we may with probability infer that Lk. regards Mary as descended from David. In ii. 4 he states this of Joseph.
what_it_says: Plummer thinks Luke 1:27, 1:32 and 1:69 imply Mary was descended from David, while 2:4 says it of Joseph.
limits: Plummer says the inference is probable, not certain (see G6-16). The first sentence is read from the djvu OCR (Greek garbled).

author: J. Gresham Machen
ref: Luke 1:27 (Lk. i.27 and the house of David)
original: Ἐν δὲ τῷ μηνὶ τῷ ἕκτῳ ἀπεστάλη ὁ ἄγγελος Γαβριὴλ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς πόλιν τῆς Γαλιλαίας ᾗ ὄνομα Ναζαρὲτ πρὸς παρθένον ἐμνηστευμένην ἀνδρὶ ᾧ ὄνομα Ἰωσὴφ ἐξ οἴκου Δαυείδ, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τῆς παρθένου Μαριάμ.
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: It seems more natural to regard them as referring to Joseph. This is so for two reasons. In the first place, the words come immediately after the name of Joseph: and, in the second place, repetition of the noun, "the virgin," would not have been necessary at the end of the verse if Mary had just been referred to in the preceding clause. [...] If so, the Davidic descent of Mary is not mentioned in the narrative. There is indeed nothing in the narrative to prevent us from holding, if we care to do so, that Mary was descended from David.
page: printed p. 127 (PDF p. 143); the OCR layer reads '727'
edition: Machen, The Virgin Birth of Christ (1930); archive.org virginbirthofchr0000jgre_h9i1
what_it_says: Machen reads 'of the house of David' as Joseph's, so the narrative does not state Mary's Davidic descent, though it does not exclude it.
limits: Machen cites the Roman Catholic counter-reading (Mary as the chief person in the sentence) and calls it worth consideration. Not Machen's last word: he later prefers the Joseph genealogy on Luke 3 (p. 204).

author: J. Gresham Machen
original: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν Ἰησοῦς ἀρχόμενος ὡσεὶ ἐτῶν τριάκοντα, ὢν υἱός, ὡς ἐνομίζετο, Ἰωσήφ τοῦ Ἡλεί
original_edition: Greek of the commented verse, see G6-01 (WH via Biblehub)
english: On the whole, however, it seems better to follow the usual view, in accordance with which the genealogy is the genealogy of Joseph. This view is in accordance with what we saw to be the more natural interpretation of Lk. 1.27.
what_it_says: Machen concludes Luke's genealogy is Joseph's, after weighing Heli as Mary's father.
limits: Machen's conclusion is the traditional reading; he states the Mary reading as 'a more natural way', then rejects it on balance.

work: A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Gospel according to St. Luke (ICC)
author: Alfred Plummer
original: καὶ ἰδοὺ συλλήμψῃ ἐν γαστρὶ καὶ τέξῃ υἱόν, καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν. οὗτος ἔσται μέγας καὶ υἱὸς Ὑψίστου κληθήσεται, καὶ δώσει αὐτῷ Κύριος ὁ θεὸς τὸν θρόνον Δαυεὶδ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ,
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS. He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:
what_it_says: The phrase 'throne of his father David' is thought to imply Mary's Davidic descent, but Plummer says the inference is not certain: Jesus was the heir of Joseph.
limits: Plummer's own statement; he treats the inference as uncertain.

work: A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Gospel according to St. Luke (ICC)
author: Alfred Plummer
original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν αὐτῇ Πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐπελεύσεται ἐπὶ σέ, καὶ δύναμις Ὑψίστου ἐπισκιάσει σοι· διὸ καὶ τὸ γεννώμενον ἅγιον κληθήσεται, υἱὸς θεοῦ· καὶ ἰδοὺ Ἐλεισάβετ ἡ συγγενίς σου καὶ αὐτὴ συνείληφεν υἱὸν ἐν γήρει αὐτῆς, καὶ οὗτος μὴν ἕκτος ἐστὶν αὐτῇ τῇ καλουμένῃ στείρᾳ·
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God. And, behold, thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren.
what_it_says: Plummer answers the Levite objection: Levites could marry other tribes, so Elisabeth (of Aaron) could be related to a Davidic family; and 1:36 does not show Mary was not of David's house.
limits: This shows only that a Levite-Davidic kinship was possible, not that Mary was Davidic. 'Syngenis' is Greek for relative, not a stated tribe.

author: Luke the Evangelist
ref: Luke 2:3-4 (Joseph of the house and lineage of David)
original: καὶ ἐπορεύοντο πάντες ἀπογράφεσθαι, ἕκαστος εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ πόλιν. Ἀνέβη δὲ καὶ Ἰωσὴφ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἐκ πόλεως Ναζαρὲτ εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν εἰς πόλιν Δαυεὶδ ἥτις καλεῖται Βηθλεέμ, διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐξ οἴκου καὶ πατριᾶς Δαυείδ,
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: And all went to be taxed, every one into his own city. And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:)
what_it_says: Luke says Joseph was of the house and lineage of David; the pronoun 'auton' is masculine and refers to Joseph.
limits: Says nothing about Mary's descent; Plummer makes the same point on this verse (p. 21).

author: (as attributed)
original: περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, τοῦ γενομένου ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυεὶδ κατὰ σάρκα, τοῦ ὁρισθέντος υἱοῦ θεοῦ ἐν δυνάμει κατὰ πνεῦμα ἁγιωσύνης ἐξ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν, Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν,
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh; And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:
what_it_says: Paul states Jesus' Davidic descent 'according to the flesh' without naming the line.
limits: Says Jesus was 'of the seed of David according to the flesh'; does not name Mary or give a genealogy.

author: (as attributed)
original: προφήτης οὖν ὑπάρχων, καὶ εἰδὼς ὅτι ὅρκῳ ὤμοσεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεὸς ἐκ καρποῦ τῆς ὀσφύος αὐτοῦ καθίσαι ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ, προιδὼν ἐλάλησεν περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τοῦ χριστοῦ ὅτι οὔτε ἐνκατελείφθη εἰς ᾅδην οὔτε ἡ σὰρξ αὐτοῦ εἶδεν διαφθοράν.
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne; He seeing this before spake of the resurrection of Christ, that his soul was not left in hell, neither his flesh did see corruption.
what_it_says: Peter says God swore to David that a descendant would sit on his throne.
limits: Peter speaks of David's oath about 'the fruit of his loins'; it is about the promise, not Mary's lineage.

author: (as attributed)
original: τούτου ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ σπέρματος κατ' ἐπαγγελίαν ἤγαγεν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ σωτῆρα Ἰησοῦν,
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: Of this man's seed hath God according to his promise raised unto Israel a Saviour, Jesus:
what_it_says: Paul says God raised up Jesus from David's seed as a Saviour.
limits: Single verse only (13:23); the preceding verse 13:22 was not fetched. Says the Saviour came of this man's seed.

author: (as attributed)
original: μνημόνευε Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐγηγερμένον ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυείδ, κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιόν μου· ἐν ᾧ κακοπαθῶ μέχρι δεσμῶν ὡς κακοῦργος. ἀλλὰ ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ οὐ δέδεται·
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: Remember that Jesus Christ of the seed of David was raised from the dead according to my gospel: Wherein I suffer trouble, as an evil doer, even unto bonds; but the word of God is not bound.
what_it_says: Timothy is told to remember Jesus, risen, 'of the seed of David'.
limits: Paul gives 'of the seed of David' as part of the gospel he preaches; no genealogy or Mary named.

author: (as attributed)
original: ἐφ' ὃν γὰρ λέγεται ταῦτα φυλῆς ἑτέρας μετέσχηκεν, ἀφ' ἧς οὐδεὶς προσέσχηκεν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ· πρόδηλον γὰρ ὅτι ἐξ Ἰούδα ἀνατέταλκεν ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν, εἰς ἣν φυλὴν περὶ ἱερέων οὐδὲν Μωυσῆς ἐλάλησεν.
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: For he of whom these things are spoken pertaineth to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at the altar. For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.
what_it_says: The writer says it is evident that the Lord sprang from Judah, a tribe of which Moses spoke nothing about priests.
limits: Hebrews says Jesus came from Judah and Moses said nothing of priests from that tribe; it does not address Mary's lineage.

author: (as attributed)
original: Ἐγὼ Ἰησοῦς ἔπεμψα τὸν ἄγγελόν μου μαρτυρῆσαι ὑμῖν ταῦτα ἐπὶ ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις. ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ῥίζα καὶ τὸ γένος Δαυείδ, ὁ ἀστὴρ ὁ λαμπρός, ὁ πρωινός. Καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ ἡ νύμφη λέγουσιν Ἔρχου· καὶ ὁ ἀκούων εἰπάτω Ἔρχου· καὶ ὁ διψῶν ἐρχέσθω, ὁ θέλων λαβέτω ὕδωρ ζωῆς δωρεάν.
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star. And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely.
what_it_says: The risen Christ speaks as 'the root and the offspring of David'.
limits: Christ calls himself 'the root and the offspring (genos) of David'; a title, not a genealogy.

author: (as attributed)
original: οὐχ ἡ γραφὴ εἶπεν ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ σπέρματος Δαυείδ, καὶ ἀπὸ Βηθλεὲμ τῆς κώμης ὅπου ἦν Δαυείδ, ἔρχεται ὁ χριστός; σχίσμα οὖν ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ δι' αὐτόν.
original_edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 text as shown on Biblehub (line labelled 'Greek NT: Westcott and Hort 1881'); copied from saved HTML of the Biblehub page
english: Hath not the scripture said, That Christ cometh of the seed of David, and out of the town of Bethlehem, where David was? So there was a division among the people because of him.
what_it_says: The crowd argues the Christ should come from David's seed and from Bethlehem.
limits: A crowd's objection, quoted from Scripture, that the Christ comes from David's seed and Bethlehem; the author adds that Jesus was from Galilee in the crowd's view.

work: De consensu evangelistarum (Harmony of the Gospels), Book II, ch. 3
author: Augustine of Hippo
original_edition: Latin not retrieved in this run (Migne PL 34 / CSEL 43 not reached).
english: ...they might easily perceive that Joseph may have had two fathers — namely, one by whom he was begotten, and a second by whom he may have been adopted. For it was an ancient custom also among that people to adopt children with the view of making sons for themselves of those whom they had not begotten.
edition: New Advent, 'Harmony of the Gospels, Book II, Chapter 3' (1602203)
what_it_says: Augustine proposes that Joseph had two fathers, one begetting and one adopting, and that Luke names the adoptive father.
limits: Latin not read. Augustine later dropped this view in favour of the levirate explanation (per the Catholic Encyclopedia 'Genealogy of Christ' summary; not checked here). Augustine does not name Mary.

work: Historia ecclesiastica (Church History), Book I, ch. 7 (Africanus' letter to Aristides)
author: Eusebius of Caesarea (quoting Julius Africanus)
original_edition: Greek not retrieved: Schwartz GCS Eusebius vols 1, 2, 4 on archive.org checked; HE 1.7 text not found in the OCR.
english: By Estha then (for this was the woman's name according to tradition) Matthan, a descendant of Solomon, first begot Jacob. And when Matthan was dead, Melchi, who traced his descent back to Nathan, being of the same tribe but of another family, married her as before said, and begot a son Eli. [...] Of these the one, Jacob, when his brother Eli had died childless, took the latter's wife and begot by her a son Joseph, his own son by nature and in accordance with reason. But according to law he was the son of Eli, for Jacob, being the brother of the latter, raised up seed to him.
edition: New Advent, Church History Book I (250101)
what_it_says: Africanus explains the two lists by a levirate marriage: Jacob and Eli were uterine brothers, and Jacob raised up seed to Eli, so Joseph was Jacob's by nature and Eli's by law.
limits: Africanus is quoted by Eusebius; this English is from Eusebius's text. Africanus does not say Mary descends from Heli. Greek not read.

work: Historia ecclesiastica (Church History), Book I, ch. 7
author: Eusebius of Caesarea
original_edition: Greek not retrieved (see G6-26)
english: For the line of descent from Solomon and that from Nathan were so involved, the one with the other, by the raising up of children to the childless and by second marriages, that the same persons are justly considered to belong at one time to one, at another time to another; that is, at one time to the reputed fathers, at another to the actual fathers. So that both these accounts are strictly true and come down to Joseph with considerable intricacy indeed, yet quite accurately.
edition: New Advent, Church History Book I
what_it_says: Eusebius says both lists are true, one by nature and one by law, and that the Solomon and Nathan lines were entangled.
limits: Eusebius is paraphrasing Africanus; it is not an independent witness. Does not state Mary's line.

work: Historia ecclesiastica (Church History), Book I, ch. 7.17
author: Eusebius of Caesarea
original_edition: Greek not retrieved (see G6-26)
english: 17. Thus far Africanus. And the lineage of Joseph being thus traced, Mary also is virtually shown to be of the same tribe with him, since, according to the law of Moses, intermarriages between different tribes were not permitted. For the command is to marry one of the same family and lineage, so that the inheritance may not pass from tribe to tribe.
edition: New Advent, Church History Book I
what_it_says: Eusebius's own comment: once Joseph's line is traced, Mary is 'virtually shown' to be of the same tribe; this is about tribe, not that Luke gives Mary's line.
limits: This is Eusebius's inference, not Africanus's text. It does not claim a Davidic Mary; it places Mary in Joseph's tribe by the law of marriage.
